item.title: An Alternative Proof of the SPR Synthesis Theorem for Polynomial Segments of Arbitrary Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.09940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any positive integer n and any two monic real Hurwitz polynomials of degree n, every convex combination of the two is Hurwitz stable if and only if there exists a common numerator of degree n that makes both endpoint transfer functions strictly positive real. We give a unified proof based on convex separation, contact interpolation, and analytic properties of weakly positive real functions.
item.dc:creator: Zhengtai Xiong, Tiancheng Xu, Xiang Ji, Guowei Dou, Long Wang, Wensheng Yu

item.title: On the multivariate hypergeometric function $F_K^{(L)}$, I
item.description: arXiv:2611.09965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, a new multivariate hypergeometric series, known as the comb function, has attracted attention in physics, particularly in the study of conformal blocks in conformal field theory. This function can be regarded as a further generalization of Appell's function $F_2$ and Saran's function $F_K$. However, except for a few known formulas, little is known about its properties. In this paper, we study its fundamental properties from a mathematical perspective, such as the region of convergence, reduction formulas, an Euler-type integral representation, and decomposition formulas. Some directions for future research and connections with other multivariate hypergeometric series originating from physics are also mentioned.
item.dc:creator: Min-Jie Luo, Shu-Ying Shen

item.title: Nonlocal bilinear differential operators induced by a third order hypermetric in $\mathbb{R}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The third order hypermetric $\rho(x,y,z)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is given by the Euclidean distance of the point $(x,y,z)\in(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$ to the diagonal $\Delta^{(3)}=\{(x,x,x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$ of $(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$. In this paper, we consider local and nonlocal fractional versions of bilinear differential operators generated by the geometry induced by $\rho(x,y,z)=\rho(0,x-y,x-z)$ instead of the usual $|(x-y,x-z)|$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. In doing so, we obtain a fractional nonlocal version $\mathbb{D}^s(f,g)$, $0<s<1$, of the Dirichlet bilinear operator $\nabla f(x)\cdot\nabla g(x)$ which converges to this classical form when the fractional parameter approaches its endpoint $s=1$. We consider both the kernel approach and the Fourier multiplier version.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Aimar, An\'ibal Chicco Ruiz, Ivana G\'omez, Joaqu\'in Toledo

item.title: Optimal orders for Hilbert-valued Littlewood--Paley functions of symmetric semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.10710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Littlewood--Paley $g$-functions associated with symmetric submarkovian semigroups and Hilbert-valued functions. For every $1<p<\infty$ and $2\le q\le\infty$, we prove \[ \norm{G_q^T(f)}{L_p(\Omega)} \lesssim\max\{p',\sqrt p\}\norm{f-F(f)}{L_p(\Omega;\mathcal{H})}, \] with the sharp order $\max\{p',\sqrt p\}$, where the implicit constant is independent of $p,q$, the underlying space $\Omega$, the semigroup $(T_t)_{t>0}$, and the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$. Compactly supported radial functions show that, for each fixed $q>2$, the large-$p$ order cannot be replaced by $p^{1/q}$ in a dimension-free heat estimate. In particular, for the case $q=2$, we answers affirmatively the question posed by Xu in his \emph{JFA} paper (2022) \cite[Problem~7]{XuJFA}. For every finite $q>2$, our lower bound gives a negative answer to the dimension-free question in Xu's \emph{JEMS} paper (2025) \cite[Problem~1.8(i)]{XuJEMS}, already for real scalar functions. Together, the upper and lower bounds establish the sharp dimension-free order $\max\{p',\sqrt p\}$ for Hilbert-valued functions.
item.dc:creator: Xudong Lai, Bo Li, Ji Li

item.title: Schauder exponential basis which is not Riesz
item.description: arXiv:2611.10799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there exists a Schauder basis $\{e^{i \lambda_n t}\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with real frequencies in $L^2(-\pi,\pi)$ which is not a Riesz basis.
item.dc:creator: Andrei V. Semenov

item.title: A Quarter-Power Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.11144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every nonempty finite set $S$ of $N$ positive integers we prove $-\min_{x\in\mathbb{T}}\sum_{s\in S}\cos(2\pi sx)\gg (N/\log(2N))^{1/4}$. The proof uses a reversible phase kernel whose one-step and two-step laws are close in total variation. Comparison of rows and a height cutoff produce a partition into pieces of bounded mean. A Fourier rounding estimate then forces many additive triples to cross the partition. Two choices of phase density yield bounds in terms of negative mass and an exact conditional-pair defect, respectively. A logarithmic refinement gives a log-free bound at low triple density. At fixed positive triple density the log-free bound is a corollary of known boundary estimates. We give a separate spectral proof using an integer difference count and a theorem of Yip.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Shankar

item.title: Fefferman-Stein Type Distribution Function Inequalities on Product Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.11186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish on $R^n\times R^m$ a Fefferman--Stein type distribution function inequality in which the nontangential maximal function of the product Poisson extension is controlled by the Lusin area integral function: \[ |\{N>\lambda\}|\le C\left(|\{A>\lambda\}|+\lambda^{-2}\int_{\{A\le\lambda\}}A^2\,dx\right). \] The central idea is to establish a local $L^2$ estimate for the radial maximal function. This yields a new proof of the corresponding one-parameter inequality, avoiding Green's formula and the treatment of sawtooth regions, and extends to the multiparameter setting.
item.dc:creator: Jiecheng Chen

item.title: Uncertainty principle on $\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.11361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes an uncertainty principle on the mixed space $\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ for $n \ge 2$. Leveraging the paraboloid restriction theorem on $\mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ derived from Barron's global-in-time Strichartz estimates for the semi-periodic Schrodinger equation, we construct measurable sets $S \subset \mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ and $A(R,\delta) \subset \mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ that form a strong $L^2$ annihilating pair, satisfying the uniform inequality $\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)} \le 3(\|f\|_{L^2((\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)\setminus S)} + \|\widehat{f}\|_{L^2((\mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)\setminus A(R,\delta))})$ for all $f \in L^2(\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)$, where the measures of $S$ and $A(R,\delta)$ can be made arbitrarily large while the constant 3 remains unchanged. As an application, we derive a two-time observability inequality for the semi-periodic Schrodinger equation under a support condition on the phase-modified solution at the first observation time.
item.dc:creator: Wenkai Gan, Yufeng Yang

item.title: The bilinear Hilbert transforms are not of restricted weak type $(1,1,1/2)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.11401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every real $\alpha\neq0,1$, we show that the bilinear Hilbert transform \[ H_\alpha(f_1,f_2)(x) =\text{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f_1(x-\alpha y)\,f_2(x-y)\,\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{y} \] fails to map $L^1(\mathbb{R})\times L^1(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ when restricted to characteristic functions of sets of positive finite measure. The counterexample is quantitative and can be realized by sets that are finite unions of intervals of a common arbitrarily small length.
item.dc:creator: Nuno J. Alves, Loukas Grafakos

item.title: Random Configurations and Fourier Decoupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.11700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use tools from high dimensional probability to analyze random configurations of balls in the context of Fourier decoupling and we answer a question on the structure of superlevel sets in the setting of decoupling due to Guth.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Mulherkar

item.title: The solution of the Bochner--Krall problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.11742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve the Bochner--Krall problem posed by Krall in 1938, extending the classification beyond regular orthogonal sequences. We classify monic polynomial sequences for which multiplying each polynomial by the variable gives a linear combination of that polynomial and the polynomials of the immediately preceding and following degrees, and whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients. Orthogonality is not assumed. The general formulation allows sequences to start at any fixed degree. In every degree beyond a fixed threshold, each sequence agrees, up to an invertible affine change of variable and monic normalization, with a Hermite, Laguerre, Jacobi or Bessel family, the monomial basis, or a finite rational Darboux transform of a Laguerre or Jacobi family. In the positive-definite case, we determine the representing measures, prove their uniqueness and specify the admissible endpoint masses. No boundedness assumption on the support or asymptotic conditions on the recurrence coefficients are imposed.
item.dc:creator: K. Castillo, B. Shapiro

item.title: Pointwise estimates for an anisotropic product type singular integral on the sphere
item.dc:creator: Ahmed A. Abdelhakim

item.title: Asymptotics of matrix orthogonal polynomials with non-scalar varying weights
item.description: arXiv:2611.12262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the $2\times 2$ matrix orthogonal polynomials $\mathbf{P}_N$ on the real line with respect to the varying weights $\mathrm{e}^{-N\mathbf{Q}(z)}\mathbf{B}(z)$, where $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are real symmetric matrix polynomials that commute with a Hermite-type matrix weight, $\mathbf{Q}$ is not scalar and $\mathbf{B}$ is positive definite. We are motivated by the non-Abelian Toda deformation of the Hermite-type weight, in the sense of Dea\~no, Morey and Rom\'an. The weight depends on $N$ through a matrix exponential that is not scalar, so that its two eigenvalues have different exponential rates. The matrix orthogonality reduces to two scalar orthogonality problems on the real line, with a varying weight that has an essential singularity at the origin. Assuming that the associated equilibrium measure is one-cut regular, we obtain the strong asymptotics of $\mathbf{P}_N$ and of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$ by the Deift-Zhou steepest descent method. Our main result is the limiting zero distribution of the entries of $\mathbf{P}_N$. These zeros are complex in general, and they accumulate on a curve where the contributions of the two eigenvalues of the weight have the same size. When this curve crosses the real segment that attracts the zeros of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$, the zeros of the entries display a critical behavior, and a positive fraction of them accumulates on this segment.
item.dc:creator: Victor Alves

item.title: Translation continuity for the local bilinear circular maximal operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.12273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a positive power translation-continuity estimate for the local bilinear circular maximal operator on the real line. More precisely, there is $\eta>0$ such that the operator applied to a translation difference in either input maps $L^8(\mathbb{R})\times L^8(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^4(\mathbb{R})$ with norm $O(|h|^\eta)$. This answers Question 6.3 in Borges's survey on bilinear spherical averages. The main step is a frequency-localized estimate for arbitrary bounded inputs. A $TT^*$ argument converts it into a linear maximal problem on the plane, associated with pairs of circles. We verify the corrected multi-parameter cinematic curvature condition of Chen, Guo, and Yang by proving an irreducibility and infinitesimal independence statement for the resulting quartic curves. Uniform algebraic sublevel estimates control the degeneracies. Interpolation also gives continuity for all finite exponents $2<p,q<\infty$, with output exponent $pq/(p+q)$.
item.dc:creator: Xuyi Wei

item.title: Global zero distribution and pluripolar exceptional cones for complex linear differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the zeros of solutions of complex linear differential equations of arbitrary order $n\ge2$ with exponential-sum coefficients. Using the initial-value space $\mathbb{C}^n$ to parametrize the solutions, we show that solutions with initial vectors outside a complete pluripolar cone of Lebesgue measure zero share an explicit common leading term for the global zero count and a common joint limit in radius and angle. The rescaled radial distance from the disk boundary has an exponential limiting distribution, while the rescaled angular deviations from each main ray are Gaussian. Inspired by logarithmic tracts in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal{B}$, we pull exterior sectors back conformally to countably many curvilinear strips extending in finitely many directions and obtain zero-counting asymptotics in each strip, although the coefficients may lie outside this class. Moreover, the asymptotic formula for the global zero count and the joint limit in radius and angle persist under arbitrary entire perturbations of strictly smaller weighted exponential type.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Li

item.title: Sharpness of the Martin-O'Bryant autoconvolution inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.12685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there does not exist a constant $c<1$ such that ${\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{2}}^2\le c\,{\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{1}}{\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{\infty}}$ holds for every nonnegative $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})\cap L^2(\mathbb{R})$.
item.dc:creator: Ton\'{c}i Crmari\'{c}, Vjekoslav Kova\v{c}, Jelena Rup\v{c}i\'{c}

item.title: Second-Order Linear $q$-Difference Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Second order $q$ difference equations arise in various areas such as basic hypergeometric series, orthogonal polynomials and the analytic theory of special functions. When the independent variable is scaled by powers of $q$ ($0<q<1$), such equations display asymptotic behaviour that differs markedly from their differential or classical difference counterparts. Our purpose is to give a complete, self contained treatment of linear, second order $q$ difference equations with divergent formal solutions, including explicit error bounds, exact resummations and Stokes phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Meikle, Adri Olde Daalhuis

item.title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. II
item.description: arXiv:2611.10790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\lambda$ denote the Liouville function, and put \[ I_\lambda(X)=\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(n)e^{2\pi i n\alpha}\right|\,d\alpha. \] In this paper, we prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log I_{\lambda}(X)}{\log X} \ge \frac{1}{3}. \]
item.dc:creator: Ben Krause, Jiangpeng Li, Yu-Chen Sun, Hui Wang

item.title: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.11461v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ ( $0<\delta<\pi$) from its finite sample data $f(j),-n\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formula have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. So far the best rate has been $$ O\biggl(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(\pi-\delta)n)\biggr). $$ We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}$ satisfying $$ c_* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2}\le \rho_{n,\delta}\le C^* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2}, \quad 0<\delta\leq\pi,\quad n\geq1, $$ where $c_*,C^*$ are positive constants independent of $n$ and $\delta$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling data. In other words, $$ \rho_{n,\delta} \asymp \frac{\tan\frac\delta 4}{\sqrt{n}}\exp\bigl(-c_\delta(\pi-\delta)n\bigr), $$ where $c_\delta$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\pi]$ and $$ \lim_{\delta\to\pi^-}c_\delta=1,\ \lim_{\delta\to 0^+}c_\delta=+\infty. $$ We also make the new finding that one can also reconstruct $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ with exponentially decaying error from one-sided sample data $f(j)$, $1\le j\le n$, and the sharp rate of approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}'$ of the optimal algorithm is $$ \rho_{n,\delta}' \asymp \sqrt{\delta/\pi}\sin^n(\delta/2). $$
item.dc:creator: Wentao Huang, Haizhang Zhang

item.title: On the sharp weak-type inequality for Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2611.11788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the weak-type $(1,1)$ norm of each classical Riesz transform $R_j$, $j=1,\dots,n$, on real-valued inputs on $\R^n$ and $\T^n$ is $\KD$. The constant $\KD=\pi^2/(8\Gcat)$, where $\Gcat$ is Catalan's constant, was obtained by Davis \cite{Davis1974} for the Hilbert transform on $\R$ and the conjugate-function operator on the circle $\T$. The Burkholder--Bellman function argument also applies to coordinate Riesz transforms of product generators. If $-L$ generates a symmetric sub-Markov semigroup on a nonzero standard $\sigma$-finite measure space $Y$, then $-\partial_x(-\partial_x^2+L)^{-1/2}$ has the same exact norm on both $\mathbb R\times Y$ and $\mathbb T\times Y$. The derivative acts in the ordinary line or circle factor, while $L$ governs the independent transverse variables. An explicit integral inequality strengthens the weak-type estimate and bounds the truncated second moment of the transform. The general theorem applies to Gaussian, Dunkl, Laguerre, Jacobi, Schr\"odinger, and Laplace--Beltrami transverse generators, finite reversible chains, and subordinated semigroups.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Ba\~nuelos, M\"ahdi Hormozi, Alexander Volberg

item.title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.12607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $\mu$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $\tau$ and $\mu$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2\tau\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_H\mu-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2\tau$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions. The absolute continuity and fibre dimension theorems extend to non-coordinate projections of products under a joint Diophantine condition with exponent $\tau$ on the logarithmic contraction ratios. These imply for all self-similar sets $K,L\subset\mathbb R$ satisfying this condition and $\dim_HK+\dim_HL>1+2\tau$, every sum $uK+L$, $u\ne 0$, has positive length, and $\dim_H(L\cap(y-uK))=\dim_HK+\dim_HL-1$ for Leb. a.e. $y\in uK+L$. The proof combines the $L^1$ Gaussian smoothing approach used in the higher dimensional case with averaging at random stopping scales with a Brownian martingale bound using It\^{o} calculus.
item.dc:creator: Xiong Jin, Tuomas Sahlsten

item.title: Budan--Fourier theorem for circuit polynomial systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12613v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a Budan--Fourier theorem for linear combinations of analytic functions whose successive Wronskians are positive: the number of zeros of $g=\sum_{k=1}^s c_kh_k$ in an interval $(a,b]$, counted with multiplicities, is bounded by the drop of the number of sign changes of the sequence of Wronskians $W(h_1,\ldots,h_{k-1},g)$ between $a$ and $b$, and the difference is even. This refines the bound $s-1$ of Koiran, Portier and Tavenas, and we show that it applies, after a suitable renumbering, to any sequence of functions satisfying Descartes' rule of signs. We then study the functions arising from polynomial systems supported on circuits, that is, systems of $n$ equations in $n$ variables with $n+2$ monomials. For these functions, we show that the Budan--Fourier bound never exceeds Descartes' bound, and we compute it at the endpoints of the interval of definition. As an application, we obtain a refinement of the optimal Descartes' rule of signs for circuits of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsg{\aa}rd: we bound the number of positive solutions whose logarithm lies in explicit polytopes, these bounds add up to at most the bound of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsg{\aa}rd, and they determine the parity of the number of positive solutions.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bihan

item.title: Global Asymptotics of a Toda Soliton Condensate with Random Scattering Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.12748v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a dense $N$-soliton condensate for the infinite Toda lattice in the limit $N \to \infty$. In contrast to previous mathematical studies of soliton gases where the norming constants are assumed to be deterministic or infinitesimal, we consider initial scattering data where both the discrete eigenvalues and the norming constants are independent random variables. The norming constants $\gamma_j$ are allowed to be arbitrarily large under a mild moment condition $\mathbb{E}[\gamma_j^\nu] < \infty$ ($\nu > 1$). Our main result is divided into two parts. First, we develop a probabilistic Riemann--Hilbert framework to show that the system self-averages: despite large, independent fluctuations in the initial data, the random Toda lattice variables converge deterministically to an effective continuum model at a polynomial rate $\mathcal{O}(N^{-\delta})$ for $0 < \delta < 1/2$. Second, by performing the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent analysis of the continuum problem, we obtain the complete leading-order macroscopic description of the lattice across the entire space-time plane. The solution decomposes into five distinct finite-gap regimes, characterized explicitly by modulated elliptic and genus-2 waves with an error of order $\mathcal{O}(1/\ln N)$. In contrast to the straight characteristic rays typical of standard soliton gas limits, the interfaces separating these five macroscopic regimes in the space-time plane are genuinely non-linear curves; in particular, the boundary of the modulated genus-2 region is completely non-linear. Finally, under our assumptions, we establish the Nonlinear Dispersion Relations for the Toda soliton condensate and prove that the macroscopic ensemble averages are determined by the soliton gas density of states.
item.dc:creator: Guido Mazzuca, Mateusz Piorkowski

item.title: Sharp endpoint $L^p$-estimates for bilinear spherical maximal functions
item.description: arXiv:2310.00425v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we address endpoint issues for the bilinear spherical maximal function. We obtain borderline restricted weak type estimates for the well studied bilinear spherical maximal function $$\mathfrak{M}(f,g)(x):=\sup_{t>0}\left|\int_{\mathbb S^{2d-1}}f(x-ty_1)g(x-ty_2)\;d\sigma(y_1,y_2)\right|,$$ in dimensions $d=1,2$ and as an application, we deduce sharp endpoint estimates for the multilinear spherical maximal function. We also prove $L^p-$estimates for the local spherical maximal function in all dimensions $d\geq 2$, thus improving the boundedness left open in the work of Jeong and Lee (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfa.2020.108629). We further study necessary conditions for the bilinear maximal function, \[\mathcal M (f,g)(x)=\sup_{t>0}\left|\int_{\mathbb S^{1}}f(x-ty)g(x+ty)\;d\sigma(y)\right|\] to be bounded from $L^{p_1}(\mathbb R^2)\times L^{p_2}(\mathbb R^2)$ to $L^p(\mathbb R^2)$ and prove sharp results for a bilinearized version of $\mathcal M$.
item.dc:creator: Ankit Bhojak, Surjeet Singh Choudhary, Saurabh Shrivastava, Kalachand Shuin

item.title: An alternate approach to bilinear rough singular integrals
item.description: arXiv:2508.19181v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of this paper is to provide a new approach to address the $L^p-$boundedness of bilinear rough singular integral operators. This approach relies on local Fourier series expansion of input functions leading to trilinear estimates with desired decay in the frequency parameter. This approach departs from the existing methods of the wavelet decomposition of the multiplier employed in the work of Grafakos, He and Honz\'ik and in a series of subsequent papers in the context of bilinear rough singular integrals. With this new approach, we prove sharp $L^p-$estimates for maximally truncated bilinear rough singular integrals when the kernel is supported away from the diagonal in the plane. Furthermore, this method allows us to deduce a new and self-contained proof of $L^p-$boundedness of the bilinear rough singular integral operators in all dimensions for the optimal range of exponents.
item.dc:creator: Ankit Bhojak, Saurabh Shrivastava

item.title: Endpoint variation and jump inequalities for rough singular integrals
item.description: arXiv:2602.21888v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we establish weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for the variation and jump operators associated with the family of truncated singular integrals with rough kernels. This resolves an open question raised by Jones, Seeger and Wright (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (2008)). Moreover, as an immediate consequence of the variational estimate, we recover the weak type $(1,1)$ boundedness of the maximally truncated rough singular integral operator.
item.dc:creator: Ankit Bhojak, Saurabh Shrivastava

item.title: Orthogonal polynomials which are eigenfunctions of a partial differential operator
item.description: arXiv:2609.01751v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study orthogonal polynomials of $d = d_1+d_2$ variables with respect to a wrapped product weight function $\Wb(\bm x,\bm y) = W_1(\bm x/\rho(\bm y)) W_2(\bm y)$ for $(\bm x, \bm y) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_1} \times \mathbb{R}^{d_2}$, where $\rho$ is either linear or the square root of a nonnegative quadratic polynomial, and identify all such polynomials that are eigenfunctions of a second-order linear differential operator. For $d =2$, it is known that there are primarily, up to affine transformations, five families of such polynomials, which are products or wrapped products of classical orthogonal polynomials of one variable; all five families have their counterparts in higher dimensions, but no characterization is known in dimension three or higher. Our study explores viable wrapped product families, finds explicit second-order differential operators for two new families of orthogonal polynomials in $d= d_1+d_2$ variables that have not been studied before when either $d_1>1$ or $d_2 > 1$, and provides, in particular, a complete list of such operators among all wrapped product orthogonal polynomials when $d = 3$. The list also includes four families that are eigenfunctions of a fourth-order differential operator, whereas no second-order operator is available. Moreover, orthogonal polynomials on the corresponding wrapped quadratic surfaces that are eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator on the surface are also studied.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Xu

item.title: On pointwise convergence of singular integrals of Christ-Journ\'e type
item.description: arXiv:2610.04673v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The primary objective of this paper is to establish the pointwise almost everywhere convergence of the singular integrals of Christ-Journ\'e type. To this end, we prove the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for the corresponding maximal operator defined as \[ T^*[a] f(x):= \sup_{r>0}\left|\int_{|x-y| > r} K(x-y) \int_0^1 a(tx + (1-t)y)\, dt f(y)\, dy\right|, \] where $K$ is a Calder\'on--Zygmund kernel and $a\in L^\infty$. This result resolves a problem posed by Seeger (Rev. Mat. Iberoam., 2014).
item.dc:creator: Ankit Bhojak, Sangita Kundu, Saurabh Shrivastava

item.title: Oscillatory Integral Operators Along the Paraboloid and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.14841v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove decay estimates for oscillatory integral operators along $(y_1, y_2, y_1^2+y_2^2)$ in the finite field and the continuous settings. In the continuous setting, our result allows a bi-parameter maximal modulation, which extends the one-parameter version previously established by Pierce and Yung. Our approach is different from theirs. Then we discuss three applications of our estimates: a power saving bound for certain pattern finding problem in finite fields, a short approach to $L^p$ boundedness of an one-parameter Pierce--Yung operator, and $L^p$ boundedness of a bi-parameter Pierce--Yung operator.
item.dc:creator: Jianghao Zhang

item.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16294v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove cone restriction estimates under half-scale dimensional conditions. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we incorporate the broad restriction estimate of Ou--Wang and a localized multilinear estimate obtained through cyclic bilinear pairing and multilinear Kakeya bounds for local packet energies. For certain ambient and weight dimensions, our estimates are sharp in suitable ranges of $p$, up to an $R^\varepsilon$ loss.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
item.description: arXiv:2610.21847v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a weak $(1,1)$ estimate for the full Poisson Littlewood--Paley $g$-function on every complete Riemannian manifold without boundary, with an explicit universal constant approximately equal to $2.06970$. The estimate requires no curvature restriction, volume doubling, heat kernel bound, or stochastic completeness. The proof combines a precise Poisson maximal inequality with a good-set energy estimate derived from a convex entropy identity. The constant is sharp for the abstract combination of these two estimates; no optimality is claimed for the operator norm. Local elliptic regularity is used to justify the passage to arbitrary real $L^1$ data. As an application, we obtain weak $(1,1)$ estimates for certain spectral multipliers represented by Poisson time derivatives with coefficients in $L^2((0,\infty),dt/t)$.
item.dc:creator: Bo Li, Ji Li, Jinxia Li

item.title: A quantitative form of the planar Falconer distance theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.22222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we prove a uniform lower bound for the length of a planar distance set under a bound on the concentration of mass. For each $0<\eta<1$, we obtain $b(\eta)>0$ such that every compact $F\subset\overline{B}(0,1)$ carrying a Borel probability $\nu$ with $\nu(B(z,r))\le2r^{1+\eta}$ for all $z\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $0<r\le1$ satisfies $|\Delta F|\ge b(\eta)$. For a compact planar set $E$ of diameter $D>0$ carrying a probability with $\mu(B(z,r))\le A(r/D)^{1+\varepsilon}$ for all centers and $0<r\le D$, where $A\ge1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, localization gives $|\Delta E|\ge c_{\varepsilon,p}DA^{-p}$ for each fixed $p>1/\varepsilon$, with $c_{\varepsilon,p}>0$ depending only on $\varepsilon$ and $p$. In particular, every compact planar set of Hausdorff dimension greater than one has a distance set of positive length. The proof uses scale-dependent cutoffs to construct approximants to a fixed positive distance measure. The same approximants have summable total-variation errors and summable integrals of the squared modulus of their Fourier transforms over the corresponding dyadic bands. We develop the multiscale method of OpenAI's release on October 6, 2026 in the plane and prove the estimates with constants uniform over the normalized family. This paper is for expository purpose only and is not intended for publication.
item.dc:creator: Guozheng Cheng, Xiang Fang, Menghan Li, Hongdou Qu, Chengbo Xiao

item.title: The Separated Orlicz Bump Theorem in $L^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35949v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a separated entropy bump theorem for two-weight $L^2$ inequalities for positive operators defined by Carleson sequences on a probability space with a general filtration. The bump conditions use conditional averages of martingale maximal functions and involve the first power of the entropy penalty, removing the square appearing in the separated condition of Treil and Volberg. As a consequence, we obtain separated Orlicz bump estimates for a class of doubling Young functions. The final section describes a direct Orlicz argument that removes the doubling assumption and the monotonicity assumption on $\frac{\Phi(t)}{t\log t}$, and discusses extensions to other exponents. These results apply, in particular, to sparse operators. The proof uses principal sequences, a natural global extension of principal sets, and combines a good-$\lambda$ estimate with a weighted Carleson embedding to obtain the required testing inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Yuekai Zhou

item.title: Sharp double logarithmic $L^\infty$ bounds for second-order Sobolev functions in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:1301.2353v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Although $W^{2,2}(\mathbb{R}^{4})$ does not embed into $L^\infty$, we prove that radial symmetry allows the $L^\infty$ norm to be controlled by the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm $\dot H^2$, at the cost of a logarithmic correction involving a stronger H\"older-type norm. Our main result is a sharp double-logarithmic inequality with optimal leading constant $1/(8\pi^2\alpha)$. We also establish a single-logarithmic estimate and prove the sharpness of its threshold. The optimal lower bound is derived by analysing a biharmonic obstacle problem with H\"older-type obstacle. A tailored penalization argument yields existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the minimizer, while an explicit transcendental equation for the free-boundary radius determines the sharp constant through its asymptotic behavior. These results provide fourth-order, four-dimensional analogues of the two-dimensional first-order inequalities of Ibrahim--Majdoub--Masmoudi (\textit{Proc.\ Amer.\ Math.\ Soc.}, 2007), with potential applications to fourth-order semilinear evolution equations with exponential nonlinearities.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Majdoub, Tarek Saanouni

item.title: Explicit expressions for iterates of power series
item.description: arXiv:2409.09809v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present several formulas for both the discrete and fractional iterates of an invertible power series $f,$ using a new unifying approach based on umbral calculus. Known formulas are extended, and their proofs simplified, while new expressions are introduced. In particular, by employing $q$-calculus identities, we eliminate the requirement for $f'(0)$ to equal $1$ and the resulting general expressions for the iterative logarithm are also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Kei Beauduin

item.title: On $q$-real and $q$-complex numbers
item.description: arXiv:2508.08440v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In arXiv:1812.00170 and arXiv:1908.04365, Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko introduced $q$-rational numbers $[x]_q$, rational functions specializing to $x$ at $q=1$, and their extension to $q$-real numbers, Laurent series agreeing with $[x]_q$ for rational $x$. It was conjectured in arXiv:2102.00891 that for every real $x>1$, $[x]_q$ has positive radius of convergence, with optimal common radius $R_*=(3-\sqrt{5})/2$, attained at the golden ratio. We prove that $[x]_q$ converges to a nonvanishing holomorphic function for every real $x>1$ and $|q|<3-2\sqrt{2}$. The proof gives an expansion of $1/[x]_q$ as a $q$-adically convergent series of rational functions, converging absolutely and locally uniformly on an explicit region. It also defines a positive analytic function for $q\in(-R_*,1)$. Using arXiv:2405.15970, we further obtain convergence for $|q|<2-\sqrt{3}$. We compute $[x]_q$ explicitly for some transcendental $x$, including ${\rm cotan}(1)$ and $e$. We also establish sharp inequalities for numerators and denominators of $q$-rationals when $|q|=1$ and determine the closure of the set of $[x]_q$ when such $q$ is not a root of unity. Next, we show that coefficientwise reduction modulo every $m\ge2$ is injective on the Cantor line (the extended real line with doubled up rationals and the Cantor set topology); for $m=2$, it identifies the Cantor line with $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_2((q)))$. We describe the inverse map, extend rationality results modulo every prime, characterize quadratic series over $\mathbb F_2(q)$ corresponding to quadratic irrationals, derive criteria for eventual parity of coefficients, and compute the real numbers corresponding to $1+q^n$. Finally, we propose a definition of $q$-complex number $[\tau]_q$, a meromorphic function in $\tau\in\mathbb C_+$ expressed via hypergeometric functions evaluated at modular functions of $\tau$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Etingof

item.title: New nonabelian Hodge graphs from twisted irregular connections
item.description: arXiv:2509.24861v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is known that any meromorphic connection on the Riemann sphere determines a finite diagram (a generalised graph, possibly with negative edge multiplicities), which is invariant under the Fourier-Laplace transform. If the connection has regular singularities at finite distance and an untwisted irregular singularity at infinity, the diagram is a supernova graph, and the quiver modularity theorem of Boalch/Hiroe-Yamakawa shows that the corresponding nonabelian Hodge moduli space contains the Nakajima quiver variety of the graph as an open subset. In this note, motivated by the question of classifying these nonabelian Hodge diagrams, we obtain a necessary condition satisfied by all (core) nonabelian Hodge diagrams, involving ultrametric inequalities. We use this to investigate the class of such diagrams that are graphs (without edge-loops nor negative multiplicities), as well as certain special classes of nonabelian Hodge graphs: we show that there exist nonabelian Hodge graphs beyond the setting of the quiver modularity theorem, and obtain characterisations of fission graphs and of simply-laced nonabelian Hodge graphs.
item.dc:creator: Jean Dou\c{c}ot

item.title: A new product formula for $(z;q)_\infty$, with applications to asymptotics
item.description: arXiv:2602.11329v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We express the $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(z;q)_\infty$ as an infinite product of gamma functions, analogously to how Narukawa expressed the elliptic gamma function as an infinite product of hyperbolic gamma functions. This identity is used to obtain asymptotic expansions when $q$ tends to $1$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Arabi Ardehali, A., Rosengren, H. A New Product Formula for $(z;q)_\infty$, with Applications to Asymptotics. Constr Approx (2026)
item.dc:creator: Arash Arabi Ardehali, Hjalmar Rosengren

item.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29211v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every open $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb{R}$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We extend our conclusions from the Euclidean metric to a general class of ambient metrics including Riemannian metrics and we establish uniform local upper bounds for the lengths of the spherical projections of gradient flow trajectories. We finally apply our findings to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).
item.dc:creator: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck

item.title: Local $Tb$ theorems with applications to the Neumann problem and caloric measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.40135v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calder\'on-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators. We obtain the following applications: - If $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq 2$, is a bounded domain with Ahlfors regular boundary satisfying the interior corkscrew condition, and the Neumann problem for the Laplacian in $\Omega$ is solvable with data in $L^p$ for some $1<p<\infty$, then $\partial\Omega$ is uniformly rectifiable. The proof applies the matrix-valued version of the theorem to the Cauchy-Clifford operator. - In the parabolic space $\mathbb{P}^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(\sigma)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $\sigma$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Merlo, Mihalis Mourgoglou, Carmelo Puliatti

item.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.01014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we investigate finite-time boundary collisions and interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. We first prove that finite-time boundary collisions are impossible for arbitrary nonzero vortex circulations, without any restrictions on their signs or algebraic relations. The result excludes both simultaneous boundary collapse and individual vortex approaches to the boundary, without requiring convergence of the vortex trajectories. In contrast, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse by treating the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gr\"{o}bli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Yang

item.title: An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
item.description: arXiv:2611.06376v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. Its remaining life expectancy has no known closed form, and numerical evaluation alone does not reveal how the immaturity hazard enters it. We show that the remaining-lifetime distribution at age $x$ is Gompertz--Makeham with a Poisson-distributed Makeham term. Successive Makeham terms differ by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines, and the Poisson mean is the cumulative immaturity hazard remaining after age $x$. In a latent-clock construction, individuals carry a Poisson number of constant-rate clocks, and selection removes those carrying more clocks first. Integrating the mixture yields an exact series for remaining life expectancy with a closed-form truncation bound. The life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality is close to the probability of carrying a clock times life expectancy with that hazard removed, with a closed-form error bound. In annual fits to Swedish female mortality, this loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, a decline equal to 15\% of the gain in life expectancy at birth, and the approximation was always within 0.06 years.
item.dc:creator: Silvio C. Patricio
